subject: US state processor boundary & evidence request
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acmecorp.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: privacy@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2025 15:22:00 -0400
Subject: US state processor boundary & evidence request

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Our legal and privacy teams are working through contract language for CCPA/CPRA and a few state-level privacy addenda. Attached is Acme's standard DPA / state annex for your review (Acme_DPA_template.pdf). Before we run it through procurement, can you confirm the following from Redwood's perspective?

- Will Redwood agree to the typical CCPA/CPRA "service provider" (processor) limited-use language (no secondary use / no sale) and accept the state annex in that form?
- Telemetry & logs: do you retain raw request logs containing client IPs, full request payloads, or other identifiers beyond transient troubleshooting? If so, what is the default retention?
- Subprocessors: please provide an up-to-date subprocessors list + SOC2 / attestation links (we need evidence for our security review).
- Transfers & residency: does processing ever involve cross-state transfers that might implicate some state statutes? Any outbound transfers outside the US we should be aware of?

We're trying to move procurement in the next 2–3 weeks. If you can send your proposed redlines and a short subprocessor matrix, that will help speed sign-off. Happy to set a 30-minute call with Acme legal if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Director, Privacy–Acme Corp
(attachment: Acme_DPA_template.pdf)

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acmecorp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Sep 2025 09:07:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: US state processor boundary & evidence request

Alex — thanks for the clear list. We can take the following positions and I attached a short DPA draft and our current subprocessor matrix for your team to review (Redwood-DPA-draft-20250925.pdf; redwood-subprocessor-matrix-20250926.csv).

High-level answers:
- Service provider role: Redwood will accept the service-provider / processor designation under US state statutes (CCPA/CPRA language) with the standard limited-use, no-sale commitments. We will sign the state annex with mutually agreed redlines.

- Telemetry & logs: default behavior is to keep transient request metadata (no full request payloads) for 30 days to support routing/diagnostics. IP addresses are hashed and retained for 7 days by default. We do persist minimal audit logs for customer-requested audit retention; that is opt-in and documented in the DPA (section 4.3).

- Subprocessors & attestation: current subprocessors are listed in the matrix; for third parties where SOC2 is available we can share the attestations or a redacted report under NDA. Major infra subprocessors (AWS, a managed logging provider) are called out and we can provide SOC2 links.

- Transfers: all customer data is processed and stored in US regions by default. We do not export customer content outside the US unless a customer requests a non-US region or there is an operational need; any such transfers are captured in the subprocessor notice and DPA clause.

Next steps I propose: 1) you run our DPA draft against Acme's template and return redlines; 2) we set a 30-minute call between Acme legal / privacy and our security/ legal to walk through retention and attestation evidence. Can you share two times next week?

Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
(attachments: Redwood-DPA-draft-20250925.pdf, redwood-subprocessor-matrix-20250926.csv)

From: connor.obrien@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Sep 2025 11:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: US state processor boundary & evidence request

Forwarding Acme's asks. Key negotiation points to be prepared for:
- They will push on telemetry retention and raw IPs — we should hold to hashed IPs + 7 day default and offer an opt-in extended audit option.
- Subprocessor evidence: provide SOC2 links where available; offer an NDA/redacted report for the logging vendor if needed.
- Notice window for subprocessor changes: they may ask for 30 days; we can offer 14 days with an opt-in for 30.

Ben / Marissa — thoughts on concessions? Also thinking we highlight that data residency is US by default and that outbound transfers require an explicit customer request.

—Connor

From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@acmecorp.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmecorp.com, privacy@acmecorp.com
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 19:40:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: US state processor boundary & evidence request

Connor — appreciate the quick turnaround and the DPA + matrix. A couple of follow-ups before we schedule legal review:

1) Can you send SOC2 Type II links (or attestations) for AWS and the logging provider? If a redacted report is necessary we can sign an NDA.
2) Confirm whether the default logs ever contain raw client IPv4/IPv6 values when the system is in standard configuration (i.e., before any customer enables extended audit logging). You mentioned hashing — does hashing occur at collection or at rest?
3) Subprocessor notice: Acme prefers a 30-day notice window for material subprocessor changes. If Redwood cannot agree to 30 days, propose a 14-day notice plus proactive email flagging for high-impact changes.

If you can drop the SOC links and a short paragraph clarifying IP handling, we'll share with procurement and legal. Also happy to set a 30-minute call; HubSpot record is ACME-98765. Proposed DocuSign packet will go after legal sign-off: https://www.docusign.com/packets/ACME-Redwood-DPA-2025

Best,
Alex Torres
Director, Privacy — Acme Corp
(related hubspot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/ACME-98765)
